inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved Slayer parent value.

profiles.name: Ankou's Shadow
profiles.sourceCitationText: Legacy of the First World pg. 14

evidence.reason: Up to four persistent shadow doubles provide flanking, aid allies and become alternate origins for attacks.
The doubles function as replenishable mirror images while sharing the Slayer’s space.
Directed doubles flank and use aid another for the Slayer and allies.
Attacks and abilities can originate from independently positioned doubles.

profiles.playerSummary: A fey-inspired assassin who fights through mobile shadow doubles that flank, assist, misdirect attacks and eventually strike independently.
profiles.tradeoff: Studied target is lost, and the doubles are fragile illusions whose positioning adds substantial play complexity.

profiles.name: Avalancher

evidence.reason: Leaping and falling become the archetype’s defining movement and attack engine.
A long descending jump can distribute a full attack across several creatures.

profiles.playerSummary: A vertical skirmisher who drops from cliffs and ledges, attacking several enemies during a single fall.
profiles.tradeoff: Its strongest bonuses require reliable elevation and safe falling routes, replacing the universally applicable studied-target engine.

profiles.name: Bloody Jake

constraints.summary: A Bloody Jake must be evil and cannot advance in the archetype after becoming nonevil.

evidence.reason: Fear, disorientation, ability damage and supernatural misdirection become recurring tools.
Ranger traps and area fear effects control terrain and groups.
Supernatural fear and terrain magic directly attack enemy effectiveness.
Ventriloquism, blindsense and tree stride add magical utility.

profiles.playerSummary: An evil backwoods predator who dominates one favored terrain with fear, snares, folk magic and sadistic sneak attacks.
profiles.tradeoff: Studied target is delayed and weakened, several talents disappear, and much of the toolkit depends on one chosen terrain and Charisma.

profiles.name: Bounty Hunter

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype is explicitly hired to capture wanted targets or debtors alive.

evidence.reason: Sneak attack converts directly into dirty tricks and enhanced grappling.
Dirty tricks and forced unconsciousness make disabling targets defining.

profiles.playerSummary: A professional captor who converts sneak attacks into dirty tricks, submission holds and nonlethal incapacitation.
profiles.tradeoff: Several flexible Slayer talents are replaced by a narrow capture-and-control package.

profiles.name: Butterfly Blade
profiles.sourceCitationText: Heroes of the High Court pg. 24

evidence.reason: Intimidation, negotiation and supernatural inconspicuousness support political infiltration.
The normal sneak-attack progression is fully replaced by butterfly-sword bonuses and knockout.

profiles.playerSummary: A courtly enforcer who intimidates nobles, appears harmless and fights nonlethally with specialised butterfly swords.
profiles.tradeoff: Sneak attack is lost and most signature combat benefits depend on one unusual weapon.

profiles.name: Cleaner

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly defines the job as destroying evidence, disposing of bodies and eliminating witnesses.

evidence.reason: The Cleaner can reconstruct, conceal or falsify physical evidence at a crime scene.
Bluff and Disguise receive explicit feat support.
At-will misdirection masks the Cleaner from divination.

profiles.playerSummary: A professional crime-scene cleaner who removes bodies, falsifies evidence, deceives investigators and masks divinations.
profiles.tradeoff: Tracking and some combat flexibility are exchanged for specialised post-crime utility.

profiles.name: Covenbane

evidence.reason: Threatened creatures cannot participate in coven powers, friendly spellcasting or teamwork.
Magical scars detect hags, spellcasters, magical disguises and invisible magical foes.

profiles.playerSummary: A scarred hunter of hags and magically linked groups who detects hidden magic and severs coven cooperation.
profiles.tradeoff: Several broadly useful Slayer features are replaced by tools strongest against spellcasters and linked enemies.

profiles.name: Cutthroat

evidence.reason: Survival and geography are removed and Track becomes an urban skill speciality.
Urban movement and opportunistic theft become supported practical tools.
Diplomacy, nobility and Linguistics receive explicit class support.

profiles.playerSummary: An urban opportunist who exploits surprise, street skills and swift theft rather than wilderness tracking.
profiles.tradeoff: Wilderness capability and several talents are traded for situational advantages in cities and surprise rounds.

profiles.name: Deliverer

constraints.summary: A Deliverer is chosen by and serves a deity.
Grossly violating the deity’s required conduct removes the archetype’s class features until atonement.

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly calls the Deliverer a divine assassin, god’s blade or wrath-bringer.

evidence.reason: Diehard, Will bonuses and continued action below zero hit points reinforce survival against moral opposites.

profiles.playerSummary: A deity’s chosen assassin who survives mortal wounds and deals divine punishment to enemies far from the Deliverer’s alignment.
profiles.tradeoff: Its strongest benefits are alignment-dependent, and violating the deity’s code removes the archetype’s powers.

profiles.name: Dune Rider

evidence.reason: Mounted speed, terrain freedom and reduced mounted-ranged penalties define the combat style.

profiles.playerSummary: A mounted desert skirmisher who rides quickly over sand and rock while delivering accurate ranged attacks.
profiles.tradeoff: Studied-target benefits become terrain-bound and peak performance requires both a mount and warm desert, hill or mountain terrain.

profiles.name: Family Hunter

evidence.reason: At-will supernatural kinship detection makes tracing one bloodline central.
Studied targets cannot flank, aid or use teamwork against the Family Hunter.
At-will discern next of kin provides supernatural investigative utility.

profiles.playerSummary: An obsessive hunter who traces one bloodline, attacks its relatives more effectively and disrupts coordinated enemies.
profiles.tradeoff: Multiple studied targets must be related, and its defining benefits depend heavily on the selected family.

profiles.name: Grave Warden

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype is explicitly dedicated to ending undead and other night-born horrors.

evidence.reason: Holy-water weapon treatment and a dedicated destruction ability provide reliable anti-undead advantages.
A repeatable holy-water ritual grants personal death ward.

profiles.playerSummary: A practical undead hunter who weaponises holy water, protects himself with death ward and destroys studied undead.
profiles.tradeoff: Its replacement features are highly specialised and consume purchased holy water.

profiles.name: Guerrilla

evidence.reason: The Guerrilla can make a full-distance charge during the surprise round.

profiles.playerSummary: An ambush specialist who remains hidden while sniping, charges immediately and prolongs vulnerability after a surprise sneak attack.
profiles.tradeoff: Tracking and late-game quarry features are exchanged for benefits concentrated in surprise and the opening round.

profiles.name: Pureblade

evidence.reason: Aberrations can be studied immediately and suffer improved critical confirmation and capstone access.
Scaling saves and limited break enchantment counter effects created by aberrations.
Detection and untrained identification make investigating aberrations central.

profiles.playerSummary: A dedicated aberration hunter who detects alien creatures, finds their weak points and resists their mental influence.
profiles.tradeoff: Several broad Slayer tools become narrow benefits that matter primarily against aberrations.

profiles.name: Sczarni Executioner

constraints.summary: A Sczarni Executioner must be evil; becoming nonevil converts the character into a regular Slayer.

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly presents these characters as professional killers hired by crime families.

evidence.reason: Sneak attacks impose a scaling sickened condition.
Diplomacy and urban criminal skills replace several wilderness skills.
Studied-target bonuses and Slayer DCs increase against humanoids and decrease against other targets.

profiles.playerSummary: An evil professional killer specialising in humanoids, painful sneak attacks and rapid assassination.
profiles.tradeoff: Performance drops against non-humanoids, wilderness skills are reduced and evil alignment is mandatory.

profiles.name: Sniper

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The named archetype is explicitly built around disabling targets with one distant shot.

evidence.reason: Range penalties are reduced and the opening unseen shot gains exceptional sneak-attack reach and damage.

profiles.playerSummary: A long-range marksman whose first unseen shot can deliver unusually distant and damaging sneak attack.
profiles.tradeoff: The strongest benefit works only on the first attack against a target completely unaware of the Sniper.

profiles.name: Spawn Slayer

evidence.reason: Size restrictions are ignored and escalating bonuses counter larger creatures’ CMB and CMD.
The capstone temporarily strips immunity, resistances, regeneration or spell resistance.

profiles.playerSummary: A specialist in bringing down enormous single foes by neutralising their size advantage and defensive abilities.
profiles.tradeoff: Only one studied target can be maintained and several advantages require Large or larger enemies.

profiles.name: Spire Diver
profiles.sourceCitationText: Pathfinder #124: City in the Deep pg. 80

evidence.reason: A full swim speed and burst swimming make underwater repositioning defining.

profiles.playerSummary: An amphibious scout and assassin who shoots bows underwater, holds breath for extraordinary periods and swims at full speed.
profiles.tradeoff: Several tracking and social studied-target benefits become aquatic advantages that are weak away from water.

profiles.name: Spiritslayer

evidence.reason: The archetype detects invisible or possessing entities and can damage and expel possessors.
Enhanced Perception pinpoints invisible, ethereal and possessing entities.
Studied incorporeal undead lose major defences against the Slayer’s attacks and precision damage.
Studied incorporeal outsiders lose major defences against the Slayer’s attacks and precision damage.

profiles.playerSummary: A hunter of invisible, possessing and incorporeal spirits who exposes them and bypasses their unusual defences.
profiles.tradeoff: Its specialised senses and combat advantages replace general talents and matter most against a narrow supernatural enemy set.

profiles.name: Stygian Slayer

evidence.reason: Arcane spell-trigger and completion access includes offensive illusion magic.
Repeated invisibility and broad illusion-item access add meaningful infiltration utility.
The Slayer can repeatedly transform into an obscuring gaseous cloud.

profiles.playerSummary: A shadow assassin with repeated invisibility, broad access to illusion items and a supernatural mist form.
profiles.tradeoff: Medium armour, shields and several talents are lost, and much of the magical breadth depends on consumable or triggered items.

profiles.name: Toxic Sniper

evidence.section: Weapon and Armor Proficiency / Sharpshooter’s Study
evidence.reason: Martial weapons and melee studied-target bonuses are lost in favour of firearms.
Limited poisoned ammunition receives increased save DCs and can trade sneak damage for still higher DCs.
The archetype gains a battered firearm, Gunsmithing and grit support.

profiles.playerSummary: A firearm assassin who delivers strengthened poisons through carefully prepared toxic shots.
profiles.tradeoff: Martial versatility and many Slayer talents are sacrificed for firearm, ammunition and poison dependence.

profiles.name: Turncoat

evidence.reason: Bluff substitutes for diplomacy and established trust becomes a devastating combat opening.
Scaling Sense Motive identifies lies and attempts to exploit the party.

profiles.playerSummary: A social deceiver who detects treachery, talks through lies and weaponises an opponent’s trust.
profiles.tradeoff: Tracking and quarry are lost for abilities that depend on conversation, attitude and betrayal opportunities.

profiles.name: Vanguard

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly describes Vanguards as battlefield commanders and capable officers.

evidence.reason: Teamwork feats and studied-target bonuses are actively granted to nearby allies.
Allies receive a direct combat bonus against the selected target.

profiles.playerSummary: A battlefield commander who shares teamwork feats and studied-target bonuses with nearby allies.
profiles.tradeoff: Tracking and early personal talents are exchanged for limited-use group coordination.

profiles.name: Velvet Blade

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly presents well-connected killers who infiltrate nobles and hire themselves out professionally.

evidence.reason: Studied-target bonuses move from combat into Bluff, Diplomacy, Disguise, Intimidate and Sense Motive.
Noble lineages and social intelligence receive scaling support.
Track and wilderness combat study are redirected toward aristocratic social infiltration.

profiles.playerSummary: A court assassin who infiltrates aristocratic society, appears harmless and turns trust into a lethal opening.
profiles.tradeoff: Studied target no longer improves attacks or damage, and medium armour, shields and wilderness tracking are reduced.

profiles.name: Witch Killer

evidence.reason: Limited spell-like effects turn a caster’s victims against the arcane enemy.
Spell sunder options, stronger concentration disruption and anti-arcane saves make magical interference central.
Arcana, Spellcraft and at-will arcane detection support locating and identifying magic.

profiles.playerSummary: A dedicated hunter of arcane casters who scents magic, interrupts spells and adopts anti-magic rage powers.
profiles.tradeoff: Studied-target flexibility and ranger combat styles are narrowed around arcane enemies.

profiles.name: Woodland Sniper

evidence.reason: Sneak attack becomes exclusively ranged, removing a defining melee damage engine.
Tree movement develops into a full climb speed and canopy traversal.

profiles.playerSummary: A forest guardian who snipes from trees, extends ranged sneak attack and moves freely through the canopy.
profiles.tradeoff: Sneak attack can never be delivered in melee, and several benefits require trees and elevated cover.
